opts: A finger-breadth above the symphysis pubis; cosmetic, rectus muscle not cut
Three centimetres below the ASIS line; straight, rectus muscle divided
A finger-breadth above the symphysis pubis; poor cosmetic result, rectus cut
In the midline below the umbilicus; cosmetic, rectus muscle not cut
exp: The Pfannenstiel incision sits a finger breadth above the pubic symphysis (low transverse); it is cosmetically good and the rectus muscle is not cut.

opts: It is an anti-D antibody that blocks fetal red-cell sensitisation
It promotes uterine contractions and cervical ripening to expel the embryo
It blocks progesterone receptors only, leaving the cervix unchanged
It prevents all uterine contraction until the cervix is fully dilated
exp: Misoprostol promotes uterine contractions and cervical ripening or softening, expelling the detached embryo.

opts: Fetal adrenal C19 → 17α-hydroxylase → DHEA/DHEA-S → placental sulphatase and aromatase → estrogen → contractility
Placental estrogen → fetal adrenal C19 → 17α-hydroxylase → DHEA/DHEA-S → placental sulphatase → contractility
Fetal adrenal C19 → placental aromatase → DHEA/DHEA-S → 17α-hydroxylase → estrogen → myometrial contractility
Placental sulphatase → fetal adrenal C19 → DHEA/DHEA-S → placental aromatase → estrogen → myometrial relaxation
exp: Fetal adrenal C19 steroids undergo 17α-hydroxylase action to DHEA/DHEA-S, then placental sulphatase and aromatase make estrogen (E1, E2, E3), which raises myometrial contractility.

opts: Oxytocin, IV fluids and drugs given; shared decision-making and plan
Antibiotics and referral details only; shared decision-making and plan
Analgesics and fluids given; discharge summary and follow-up plan
Tocolytics and drugs given; newborn care and feeding plan recorded
exp: Section 6 of the Labour Care Guide records medication (oxytocin, IV fluids, drugs) and Section 7 records shared decision-making – assessment and plan.

opts: Maternal TSH crossing the placenta and damaging the cytotrophoblast
Placental thrombosis and infarction causing uteroplacental insufficiency
Placental overperfusion from failure of physiological conversion
Fetal hyperinsulinaemia from transplacental maternal antibody transfer
exp: Placental thrombosis in APS causes abortion, uteroplacental insufficiency with IUGR, and preterm labour.

opts: T10 level; sensory and sympathetic block without motor block
T4 level; motor and sensory block without sympathetic block
L1 level; sympathetic block only, with no sensory block
S2 level; dense motor block with no sensory or sympathetic block
exp: Epidural analgesia in labour aims at a T10 level with sensory and sympathetic block but no motor block.

opts: Valproic acid (sodium valproate)
Levetiracetam in monotherapy
Lamotrigine in monotherapy
Carbamazepine in monotherapy
exp: Valproic acid (sodium valproate) carries the highest risk of major congenital malformations, including neural tube defects, craniofacial and cardiac anomalies, and developmental delay.

opts: Acardiac acephalus (lower body developed); acardiac amorphous (no formed parts)
Acardiac acephalus (lower body developed); acardiac anceps (head formed only)
Acardiac amorphous (no formed parts); acardiac acephalus (lower body developed)
Acardiac anceps (head formed only); acardiac amorphous (no formed parts)
exp: Outcomes in the acardiac twin of TRAP are acardiac acephalus, in which only the lower part is developed, and acardiac amorphus, an amorphous mass with no formed parts.

opts: Stopping oxytocin and giving uterine relaxants; a vertical (Kronig) lower-segment incision
Continuing oxytocin to overcome the ring; a vertical (Kronig) lower-segment incision
Stopping oxytocin and giving uterine relaxants; a transverse lower-segment incision
Manual dilatation of the constriction ring; a classical upper-segment fundal incision
exp: Schroeder's ring is relieved by stopping oxytocin and giving uterine relaxants such as terbutaline; if caesarean is needed the incision is a vertical (Kronig) lower vertical incision.

opts: 20-28 weeks: misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV, then 400 mcg 3-hourly; over 28 weeks: ripen then oxytocin
20-28 weeks: oxytocin infusion alone; over 28 weeks: misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV 3-hourly
20-28 weeks: mifepristone alone; over 28 weeks: caesarean section in every case
20-28 weeks: misoprostol 25 mcg PV; over 28 weeks: misoprostol 800 mcg 3-hourly
exp: For IUD, at 20-28 weeks give misoprostol 600-800 mcg PV then 400 mcg 3-hourly; beyond 28 weeks give 25 mcg misoprostol to ripen the cervix and then oxytocin.

opts: It is the narrowest portion and slows the passage of the ovum
It has the poorest blood supply and is prone to ischaemia
It is an anatomical sphincter that traps the fertilised ovum
It is the site of fertilization and has the maximum mucosal plicae
exp: The ampulla is the site of fertilization and has the most mucosal plicae, making it the commonest tubal ectopic site.

opts: A reassuring compensatory response of a healthy fetus to transient cord occlusion
An ominous sign of impending fetal cardiac arrest and hypoxic decompensation
An artifact produced by maternal coughing or movement during the recording
Evidence of fetal seizure activity from cortical irritation by hypoxia
exp: Shoulders are transient accelerations before and after a variable deceleration, a reassuring feature signalling intact fetal autonomic responsiveness and good prognosis.

opts: The regimen requires assessment of completion and timely management of failure
Follow-up visits make mifepristone act faster and shorten the bleeding
Follow-up prevents all bleeding after the expulsion is complete
Follow-up attendance is what confirms the pregnancy is still live
exp: Medical abortion needs assessment that expulsion is complete and timely management of failure, so the woman must be able to comply with follow-up.

opts: Respiratory depression progressing to respiratory arrest
Loss of the knee jerk with reflexes otherwise preserved
Cardiac arrhythmia with a normal respiratory rate
Normal deep tendon reflexes with no change in respiration
exp: At about 12 mEq/L of magnesium, respiratory depression and then respiratory arrest occur.

opts: Transvaginal ultrasound, to measure the distance between external and internal os
Transabdominal ultrasound, to measure the distance between external and internal os
Transvaginal ultrasound, to grade the degree of placental calcification
MRI of the pelvis, to measure the distance between external and internal os
exp: The investigation of choice in placenta previa is transvaginal ultrasound, which gives the exact distance between the external and internal os.

opts: Atonic uterus : perineal tear or rupture : bleeding disorders : retained placental tissue
Retained placental tissue : atonic uterus : perineal tear or rupture : bleeding disorders
Bleeding disorders : retained placental tissue : atonic uterus : perineal tear or rupture
Perineal tear or rupture : bleeding disorders : atonic uterus : retained placental tissue
exp: The 4 Ts: Tone – atonic uterus (commonest overall and commonest primary PPH); Trauma – perineal or cervical tear, hematoma, rupture; Thrombin – bleeding disorders; Tissue – retained placental tissue (commonest secondary PPH).

opts: Old: at least 1 cm/hr, the basis of the action line; New: under 1 cm/hr can be normal
Old: at least 2 cm/hr, the basis of the action line; New: under 1 cm/hr can be normal
Old: at least 1 cm/hr, the basis of the action line; New: alert and action lines retained
Old: under 1 cm/hr was normal; New: at least 1 cm/hr with the alert line retained
exp: The old WHO recommendation was a minimum of 1 cm/hr, the basis of the action line; the new guidance accepts that under 1 cm/hr can be normal and removes the alert and action lines from the Labour Care Guide.

opts: 10 cm; below 10 cm means contracted pelvis
11 cm; below 11 cm means contracted pelvis
12 cm; below 12 cm means contracted pelvis
9 cm; below 9 cm means contracted pelvis
exp: The critical obstetric conjugate is 10 cm, and below it the pelvis is contracted and vaginal delivery impossible.

opts: Supine with 15° left lateral tilt; elective caesarean at 39 weeks
Supine with 15° left lateral tilt; elective caesarean at 37 weeks
Lithotomy position with a pelvic wedge; elective caesarean at 39 weeks
Right lateral tilt with a wedge under the hip; elective caesarean at 40 weeks
exp: The ideal position for caesarean is supine with 15° left lateral tilt or a wedge under the right hip, and elective caesarean for non-medical reasons is timed at 39 weeks.

opts: No mechanism of labour, so caesarean; early labour may convert to face or vertex
No mechanism of labour, so caesarean; early labour always converts to vertex
Manual conversion to a vertex presentation, then vaginal delivery in every case
A vacuum is applied to the brow for an immediate vaginal delivery in all cases
exp: Brow presentation has no mechanism of labour, so delivery is by caesarean section; in early labour one may wait and watch, since complete extension (face) or flexion (vertex) may still occur.

opts: Only a previous molar pregnancy, to prevent trophoblastic disease
A history of painless second-trimester abortion or of preterm labour
Only a previous normal term delivery, to shorten the latent phase
Only an Rh-negative pregnancy, to prevent maternal sensitisation
exp: In the source plan progesterone is used in a woman with a history of painless second-trimester abortion or preterm labour.

opts: Continue pregnancy to attain fetal lung maturity without risking the mother
Terminate the pregnancy immediately by caesarean section in every case
Delay delivery until beyond 40 completed weeks regardless of bleeding
Avoid antenatal corticosteroids and transfuse only when symptomatic
exp: In placenta previa with active bleeding, expectant management aims to continue pregnancy to attain fetal lung maturity without risking the mother's life.

opts: A deflexed head, which increases the presenting diameter
Placenta previa occupying the lower uterine segment
A contracted pelvis with a reduced obstetric conjugate
Polyhydramnios that prevents engagement of the presenting part
exp: The commonest cause of a free-floating head at term in a primigravida is a deflexed head, which increases the presenting diameter.

opts: Sagittal suture anteroposterior, rotation up to 45°, station at least +2
Sagittal suture anteroposterior, rotation up to 45°, station above +2
Any occipito-transverse position, rotation up to 45°, station at +2
Sagittal suture transverse, rotation up to 45°, station at least +2
exp: A favourable position for instrumental delivery is the sagittal suture in the anteroposterior diameter with rotation of at most 45° (DOA, DOP, ROA, LOA) and station +2 or more.

opts: Hyperammonaemia with mental confusion and hypoglycaemia
Hypertension alone, with no other metabolic disturbance
The degree of proteinuria, which is heavier in HELLP
A normal blood glucose level with preserved liver function
exp: Hyperammonaemia with mental confusion and hypoglycaemia favour AFLP over HELLP syndrome.

opts: To cut short the maternal bearing-down efforts that cause cardiac workload swings
To prevent fetal macrosomia and the obstructed labour that it would cause
Because cardiac drugs cause complete paralysis of the uterine muscle
Because cardiac patients cannot feel uterine contractions at all
exp: Instrumental delivery is planned to cut short and eliminate strenuous maternal bearing-down (Valsalva) efforts, which produce sharp cardiac workload swings and protect the heart from acute preload surges.

opts: PPH, DIC from thromboplastin release, and preterm labour
Placenta previa in a subsequent pregnancy, but nothing else
Vasa previa with rupture of fetal vessels in labour
Uterine inversion from traction on the placental site
exp: Abruptio placenta is associated with increased chances of PPH, DIC (from release of thromboplastin) and preterm labour.

opts: Unequal placental sharing and unequal splitting of the cell mass
Deep vascular anastomoses with artery-to-artery connections
Maternal diabetes causing symmetrical overgrowth of both twins
Cord entanglement restricting blood flow to one twin only
exp: The listed causes of selective IUGR are unequal placental sharing and unequal splitting of the initial cell mass.

opts: Slightly dilated cervix; detaching membranes releases prostaglandins and ripens
Closed cervix; stretching the membranes releases oxytocin and ripens
A fully effaced cervix; sweeping deliberately ruptures the membranes
Any cervical state; sweeping mechanically dilates the cervical canal
exp: Sweeping (stripping) of membranes is done when the cervix is slightly dilated; detaching the membranes from the cervix releases prostaglandins and ripens it.

opts: Parenteral iron replenishes stores rapidly, whereas oral iron takes 4-6 weeks
Oral iron is contraindicated in pregnancy after 34 weeks of gestation
Parenteral iron induces spontaneous cervical ripening before delivery
Parenteral iron crosses the placenta faster and corrects fetal anaemia
exp: Parenteral iron replenishes iron stores rapidly and covers the calculated deficit before delivery, whereas oral iron takes 4-6 weeks to achieve an adequate hemoglobin rise.

opts: Routine fetal movement counting from 28 weeks of gestation onwards
Normal glycosuria detected on routine antenatal urine testing
Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, molar pregnancy or chorionic-villus sampling
Normal nausea and vomiting limited to the first trimester alone
exp: First-trimester indications for anti-D prophylaxis include abortion, ectopic pregnancy, molar pregnancy and chorionic-villus sampling.

opts: Spontaneous rotation to cephalic or breech after 34 weeks; prematurity overall
Persistent transverse lie needing caesarean; uterine fibroid overall
Cord prolapse once membranes rupture; multiple pregnancy overall
Obstructed labour if untreated; cephalopelvic disproportion overall
exp: In transverse lie the commonest outcome is spontaneous rotation to cephalic or breech after 34 weeks; the commonest cause overall is prematurity, and at term it is placenta previa.

opts: Cranial nerve VIII damage causing permanent hearing loss and vestibular toxicity
Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus in the third trimester
Phocomelia and amelia from inhibition of early limb-bud development
Ebstein anomaly of the tricuspid valve with neonatal cyanosis
exp: Maternal aminoglycosides (streptomycin, gentamicin) damage the 8th cranial nerve, causing permanent sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular ototoxicity.

opts: Prolonged slow progress of labour; augmentation with ARM and oxytocin
Fetal distress from reduced perfusion; tocolysis with terbutaline
Precipitate labour with rapid delivery; tocolysis and bed rest
Uterine rupture with severe pain; immediate caesarean section
exp: Hypotonic contractions lead to prolonged or slow progress of labour and are managed by augmentation with artificial rupture of membranes and oxytocin.

opts: It increases fetal haemolysis, clearing Rh-positive cells from the circulation
It converts the fetal Rh type from positive to negative while in utero
It neutralises Rh-positive fetal red cells before maternal antibodies form
It stimulates the mother to produce her own protective anti-D antibodies
exp: Externally administered anti-D neutralises Rh-positive fetal red cells before the maternal immune system mounts stimulation and forms excess antibodies.

opts: Cervical cerclage with bed rest until term
Middle cerebral artery Doppler surveillance only
Medical abortion or suction evacuation of the uterus
Reassurance and expectant management without intervention
exp: Missed abortion can be managed with medical abortion or suction evacuation.

opts: Transvaginal ultrasound at 10-14 weeks of gestation
Transabdominal ultrasound at 20-24 weeks of gestation
Magnetic resonance imaging at 28 weeks of gestation
Umbilical artery Doppler at 16 weeks of gestation
exp: Chorionicity is best determined by transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) at 10-14 weeks in the first trimester.

opts: Anthropoid pelvis, where the AP diameter exceeds the transverse
Android pelvis, where the transverse diameter exceeds the AP
Platypelloid pelvis, where the AP diameter is markedly reduced
Gynaecoid pelvis, where all diameters are round and roomy
exp: Posterior rotation (ROP to DOP) is most commonly seen with the anthropoid pelvis, in which the AP diameter greatly exceeds the transverse.

opts: 0 or × for none; +1, +2, +3 for degrees of overlapping of cranial bones
0 or × for none; +1, +2, +3 for degrees of caput succedaneum
A, B and C grades for degrees of overlapping of the cranial bones
I, C, M and B grades recorded against each hourly observation
exp: On the partograph, moulding is recorded as 0 or × for none and +1, +2, +3 for increasing degrees of overlapping of the cranial bones.

opts: 4-5 lakh, that is 400,000-500,000 follicles
1-2 million, that is 1,000,000-2,000,000 follicles
6-7 million, that is 6,000,000-7,000,000 follicles
10,000, that is ten thousand follicles only
exp: By puberty the ovarian follicular pool is further reduced to 4-5 lakh (400,000-500,000) follicles.
